definition: Language technology, often called human language technology (HLT), studies methods of how computer programs or electronic devices can analyze, produce, modify or respond to human texts and speech.
details: Working with language technology often requires broad knowledge not only about linguistics but also about computer science. It consists of natural language processing (NLP) and computational linguistics (CL) on the one hand, many application-oriented aspects of these, and more low-level aspects such as encoding and speech technology on the other hand. Note that these elementary aspects are normally not considered to be within the scope of related terms such as natural language processing and (applied) computational linguistics, which are otherwise near-synonyms. As an example, for many of the world's lesser-known languages, the foundation of language technology is providing communities with fonts and keyboard setups so their languages can be written on computers or mobile devices. Other tools are also part of modern language technology and include machine translation, speech recognition, text processing and natural language processing. Large-scale AI models have recently advanced the field and enhanced the ability of machines to interpret complex human context.

explainer.lead: Language technology, also called human language technology, studies how computer programs and devices analyze, produce, modify or respond to human text and speech. It matters because it spans both high-level NLP and computational linguistics and low-level concerns such as encoding and speech technology.

tiers.eli5: It's the whole field of getting computers to work with human language, from typing and speech to the character codes underneath.
tiers.practitioner: Work in the field requires both linguistics and computer science knowledge, and practitioners combine NLP and computational linguistics with application-oriented and lower-level engineering. A pitfall is treating encoding and speech technology as outside scope when they are part of the field, even if related terms like NLP exclude them.
tiers.paperLevel: Language technology encompasses natural language processing and computational linguistics, their application-oriented aspects, and lower-level aspects such as encoding and speech technology; these elementary aspects are normally not considered within the scope of NLP and computational linguistics.

explainer.example: A speech-to-text product draws on language technology across levels: audio processing, text encoding, and linguistic analysis of the output.
